speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have been experiencing episodic cough and shortness of breath; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have a history of asthma or allergies?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion you experienced 8 weeks ago, followed by a one-month history of cough worsening at night and with exertion, were you prescribed any antibiotics or specific inhalers during that initial illness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodic cough and shortness of breath. I also have Cough worsens with exertion and at night, History of recent upper respiratory tract infection symptoms such as fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Cough (likely following a recent upper respiratory infection).

Given the recent URI symptoms and the nature of your cough worsening at night and with exertion, I want to confirm if you have any risk factors for tuberculosis or lung cancer, such as smoking history or recent close contact with someone who has TB. Also, have you had any hemoptysis (coughing up blood) or unexplained weight loss recently?
